records.name: Milda
records.evidence_locations: Siliņš 1990 printed p240 (PDF243), exact headword Milda, all alternatives retained; period III frequency is the highest in the entry.
records.facts_used: Klāvs Siliņš’s dictionary (1990) gives several explanations for Milda: German mild, ‘gentle’; a shortening of Emīlija, Matilde or Miranda; and the imagined Lithuanian love goddess Milda. records.name: Viia
records.evidence_locations: Rajandi PDF154/printed156, Sofia entry (text layer). Mägiste 1929 “Viia (Wd., = Sofiie)” and Mägiste 1936 PDF35 “Viia Wied.” agree. Original image not separately inspected; two independent scans of Mägiste agree.
records.facts_used: Edgar Rajandi lists Viia, with Viio ~ Viiu, as an Estonian folk short form of Sophia, Greek for ‘wisdom’, whose earlier Estonian calendar forms were Sohwi and Sohwiia on 15 May. Julius Mägiste likewise records Viia as Sophie from Wiedemann’s dictionary. Rajandi adds that in Tartu a century before his book, in 1862, the full name was given three times among 174 baptised girls, alongside one Sohvi and three Wio. He describes these forms as out of use by the 1960s.
